title: Limestone cube erosion study on the Smithsonian roof
summary: Randall Carlson tells of Limestone cube erosion study on the Smithsonian roof, about Over many decades at Washington, D.C., and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: like they they took a one cube of freshly cut limestone and they put it on the roof of the Smithsonian Institution and then began to monitor its erosion over many decades.

plain: A researcher named Randall Carlson, speaking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, describes an experiment at the Smithsonian Institution, the big national museum and research body in Washington, D.C. He says scientists put a freshly cut cube of limestone on the Smithsonian's roof and watched how it wore away over many decades. He tells it as a way of showing how fast stone actually erodes, which matters if you are trying to judge how old weathered stonework is.
